slides.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
slides.tldr: SCALING LLMS IMPROVES SOCIAL SIMULATION FIDELITY
slides.highlight: This research examines how compute scaling affects the fidelity of LLM-based social simulations, providing insights for the agent models used in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Scaling compute generally improves LLM social simulation, but fails for specific cognitive biases and underrepresented populations.
card.key_idea: The authors used compute scaling laws (85 Qwen3 models) and observational laws (35 open-weight models) to link pre-training scale to simulation fidelity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on World Values Survey, Psych-101, and ACL datasets using loss and accuracy; results show strong log-linear scaling for most tasks.
card.limitation: Scaling fails to improve calibration for human cognitive biases (e.g., risk aversion) and tasks involving correlated reward heuristics.

slides.title: UBTech Unveils Humanoid Robot Companion with Lifelike Skin and Emotional AI
slides.highlight: The development of a humanoid companion featuring lifelike skin and emotional AI is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: China Unveils Humanoid Companion Robots for Social Interaction and Domestic Assistance
slides.tldr: HUMANOID COMPANION ROBOTS FOR SOCIAL INTERACTION
slides.highlight: The development of humanoid companion robots for social interaction and domestic assistance aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Understanding LLM Intervention Explanations in Multi-Party Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research explores how LLM-based orchestrators justify decisions to intervene in multi-party human-robot interactions, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: LLM-driven robots in multi-party settings act primarily as facilitators, prioritizing agreement and participation balance.
card.key_idea: An LLM orchestrator manages two robots (mover/opposer roles), generating textual explanations for its real-time decisions to intervene in human group negotiations.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of 610 explanations from 24 groups (66 students) using a between-subjects study with homogeneous and heterogeneous role configurations.
card.limitation: Did not evaluate if explanations were understandable to users or link robot behaviors to objective task success rates.

slides.title: TurnNat: Automatic Evaluation of Turn-Taking Naturalness in Dyadic Spoken Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces TurnNat, a likelihood-based framework to automatically evaluate turn-taking naturalness in dyadic dialogue, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: TurnNat automatically evaluates turn-taking naturalness in dyadic dialogue using future voice-activity likelihoods.
card.key_idea: A causal model predicts future two-speaker voice-activity states; negative log-likelihoods (NLL) are aggregated over turn-taking boundary units (TBUs) to score conversational timing atypicality.
card.evaluation: Tested on a human-validated perturbation benchmark (Seamless Interaction dataset). Best DualTurn-based model achieved 88.0% matched-pair accuracy and 0.676 C-index.
card.limitation: Focuses on voice activity, potentially ignoring lexical content, discourse intent, and system-side failures like ASR errors or semantic misunderstandings.

slides.title: LLM-Powered Interactive Robotic Action Synthesis from Multimodal Speech, Gestures, and Music
slides.highlight: This framework uses LLMs to synthesize robotic actions from speech, gestures, and music, supporting the RwB goal of creating fluid and context-aware human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A framework using LLMs to synthesize quadruped robot actions from speech, hand gestures, and music beats.
card.key_idea: Processes multimodal inputs via Whisper (speech), gesture recognition, and beat detection, using a small LLM (Qwen3:0.6b) to map these to a predefined safe action space.
card.evaluation: Validated on a Unitree Go2 quadruped robot through preliminary experiments, such as executing a handstand triggered by a gesture and music beat.
card.limitation: Initial results are based on preliminary experiments; future work is needed to expand the action space and optimize real-time responsiveness.

slides.title: REPAIR-Bench: A Benchmark for Robot Error Perception And Interaction Recovery
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR ROBOT FAILURE PERCEPTION AND RECOVERY
slides.highlight: This benchmark introduces a framework for evaluating how users perceive robot failures and predicting preferred recovery strategies, supporting the development of trustworthy social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: REPAIR-Bench is a multimodal benchmark for detecting, classifying, and predicting recovery strategies for robot failures.
card.key_idea: It uses Hierarchical Recurrent Neural Networks (HRNN) for visual failure detection/classification and QLoRA-tuned Small Language Models (Mistral-7B, Gemma-9B) for predicting user-preferred recovery strategies.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 184 interaction trials using F1-score, Hit@k, and localization error; HRNN achieved 0.80 strict F1 for detection.
card.limitation: Small sample size (184 trials) may limit generalizability, and recovery strategies were restricted to a predefined set.

slides.title: SICAGE: Speaker-Independent Culture-Aware Gesture Generation using TED4C-L Dataset
slides.highlight: SICAGE introduces a framework for generating culturally appropriate gestures that are independent of speaker identity, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and group norms.

card.one_liner: SICAGE generates culture-aware co-speech gestures using speaker-independent embeddings to avoid confounding individual style with culture.
card.key_idea: A modular framework using Fishr regularization or adversarial learning to extract speaker-invariant cultural embeddings from audio/text, conditioning a real-time diffusion generator called ALaDiT.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new TED4C-L dataset (106h, 4 cultures) using FGD, SRGR, BAS, and a user study; ALaDiT-FI outperformed MDM and DSG+ baselines.

slides.title: From Technical Metrics to User Perception: A User Study of a Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction System for Object Detection and Grasping
slides.tldr: USER PERCEPTION OF MULTIMODAL HRI IMPROVEMENTS
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that technical gains in task success for object-grasping systems are perceptible to users, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A user study confirms that a 15% increase in robot task success is perceptible to human users.
card.key_idea: Comparing a baseline HRI system (Florence-2, LLaMA 3.1) against an improved version (Grounding DINO+SAM, Qwen 3.5 9B) using a within-subject user study on object grasping.
card.evaluation: 24 participants rated speed, reliability, and competence via 7-point Likert scales. Results show significant preferences and higher ratings for the improved system (p < 0.001).
card.limitation: Despite improvements, reliability ratings remained near the scale midpoint, indicating the system is not yet fully dependable for real-world deployment.
